Hi all — Rishi here from Security. I reviewed AtlasFin's redline and Grace's proposed TOMs draft. High-level observations and proposed edits:

- BYOK options: We support two modes: 1) HSM-backed BYOK (customer generates/holds keys in their HSM and we integrate via wrapped keys + PKCS#11 import) and 2) customer-managed KEK stored in a cloud KMS with customer control over rotation. Both require an initial key import flow and a documented emergency key rotation/handoff procedure.

- Scope of BYOK: To limit operational risk we'll propose scope language that BYOK applies to "customer-designated datasets and encrypted artifacts" (we'll specify the dataset IDs in an appendix rather than the main body). This prevents global outages caused by keys covering system-critical config.

- Key custody & recovery: AtlasFin asked about escrow — we do not recommend third-party escrow by default. Instead we can offer a documented recovery process: dual-control access with client-approved recovery officers, out-of-band verification, and optional escrow under an addendum for regulated customers (separate fees).

- Cross-border processing: We'll propose a notice-and-block mechanism. If processing must be routed outside an agreed region, Redwood will notify AtlasFin 10 business days before and provide an emergency stop if AtlasFin objects. For real-time low-latency fallbacks we can provision regional GPUs under Dedicated for an SLA-backed routing option (ops-runbook required).

- TOMs edits: I made inline suggestions in the attached TOMs exhibit (redwood-proposed-toms-exhibit_v2.docx). Key changes: explicit encryption algorithm references (AES-256-GCM at rest, TLS1.3 in transit), KMS roles/ACLs for Red Team access, logs retention window for key operations, and incident escalation matrix.

I'll copy below key snippets for quick visibility. If AtlasFin wants HSM BYOK we should schedule a 30-minute tech call next week with our infra team to validate PKCS#11 flow.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security — Redwood Inference
